articles.title: Lucky Strike Entertainment Posts $1.25B Revenue in FY2026, Remains in the Red
articles.summary: Lucky Strike Entertainment Corp reported full-year revenue of $1.25 billion for FY2026 but posted an EPS of negative $0.33, signaling continued profitability challenges for the bowling and entertainment giant. The results offer a key financial benchmark for the broader FEC and eatertainment sector. Operators and investors will be watching closely to see how Lucky Strike navigates cost pressures while sustaining top-line growth.

articles.title: Dave & Buster's Bolsters Executive Team to Drive Growth and Innovation
articles.summary: Dave & Buster's has announced additions to its senior leadership team aimed at accelerating growth, improving operational excellence, and advancing innovation across its venue portfolio. Leadership changes at the industry's largest eatertainment chain often signal strategic pivots that ripple across the FEC sector. Competitors and suppliers should monitor how the new team shapes pricing, tech investment, and format decisions.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Intensifies $13.3 Billion Indoor Entertainment Center Buildout
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia is accelerating a massive $13.3 billion investment in indoor entertainment centers as part of its Vision 2030 diversification push, representing one of the largest FEC development programs in the world. The scale of development creates significant opportunities for attraction suppliers, operators, and technology providers looking to enter or expand in the Middle East. FEC brands with scalable concepts should take note of this rapidly growing market.

articles.title: Semnox and Lumos Partner on Custom RFID Redemption System for Multi-Attraction FEC
articles.summary: Texas FEC Lumos worked with Semnox Solutions to build a bespoke RFID cashless system that integrates with a proprietary redemption platform across its arcade, bowling, axe-throwing, and laser tag offerings. The custom integration reduces guest friction and streamlines staff operations, going well beyond off-the-shelf cashless solutions. This case study illustrates how FEC operators can leverage technology partnerships to differentiate the guest experience.

articles.title: Semnox's RFID Cashless Platform Powers Multi-Attraction Venue Lumos Since Launch
articles.summary: InPark Magazine highlights how Lumos, a Texas entertainment venue featuring arcade, bowling, and laser tag, has deployed Semnox Parafait RFID cashless technology across all its attractions since opening in October 2025. The deployment features custom integrations with Lumos's proprietary redemption system, showcasing a more tailored approach to cashless guest management. This is a useful reference point for FEC operators evaluating next-generation cashless infrastructure.

articles.title: Skyline Social's 100,000 Sq Ft Minnesota FEC Selects Intercard for Arcade Cashless System
articles.summary: The new Skyline Social & Games in Apple Valley, Minnesota — a nearly 100,000-square-foot indoor and outdoor family entertainment center — has chosen Intercard's cashless technology to manage its arcade operations. The venue is operated by the Kolquist family, experienced bowling center operators making a move into the broader FEC format. The partnership underscores the growing role of proven cashless platforms in large-format FEC openings.

articles.title: $50M EVO Entertainment Destination Breaks Ground in Downtown Clearwater
articles.summary: A site has been cleared for a $50 million EVO Entertainment destination in downtown Clearwater, Florida, signaling continued major capital investment in large-format eatertainment venues. EVO's expansion reflects the growing trend of mixed-use entertainment concepts anchoring downtown revitalization projects. FEC operators and developers should track EVO's format and footprint as a model for urban entertainment destinations.

articles.title: Slick City Brings Its Dry-Slide Indoor Park Concept to Europe with 50,000 Sq Ft Nottingham Venue
articles.summary: Slick City Action Park, which has over 40 US locations, opened its first European venue in Nottingham, UK, featuring 16 high-speed dry slides and a UV AirGlider aerial attraction across 50,000 square feet. CEO Bron Launsby, a trampoline park veteran, discusses how Slick City is positioning itself as a new category of indoor attraction amid the maturing trampoline park market. The international expansion signals strong investor confidence in dry-slide as a scalable FEC format.

articles.title: Texas' Largest Family Entertainment Center Set to Open in Houston in 2026
articles.summary: A new venue billing itself as Texas' largest family entertainment center is scheduled to open in Houston in 2026, adding a major new competitor to one of the country's most active FEC markets. Large-format venues continue to raise the bar for guest experience and amenity mix in competitive metro markets. Houston-area operators and suppliers should assess the potential market impact of this opening.

articles.title: Bowling Centers Market Projected to Grow at 4.5% CAGR
articles.summary: A new market report projects the global bowling centers market will expand at a compound annual growth rate of 4.5%, reflecting sustained consumer demand for bowling as both a recreational and eatertainment anchor. The forecast supports continued investment in bowling as a core FEC attraction, particularly in hybrid entertainment venues. Operators considering bowling as a format anchor or add-on will find the growth trajectory encouraging.

articles.title: Mr. Gatti's Pizza Eyes FEC Comeback in Lubbock with New Entertainment Center
articles.summary: Mr. Gatti's Pizza is targeting a return to the Lubbock, Texas market with a new family entertainment center format combining dining and play attractions. The brand's FEC-focused revival strategy reflects the broader industry trend of pizza-and-play concepts repositioning for modern family entertainment demand. Franchisees and investors evaluating food-anchored FEC formats should watch this development closely.

articles.title: Mr. Gatti's Pursues Franchise Expansion with FEC-Focused Entertainment Center Model
articles.summary: Franchising.com reports that Mr. Gatti's is actively seeking franchisees to expand its family entertainment center concept, combining pizza dining with arcade and attraction offerings. The brand is leveraging its legacy name recognition to compete in the growing eatertainment segment. This franchise push may appeal to operators looking for a proven brand platform in the food-plus-entertainment space.

articles.title: accesso's Lee Cowie on AI, Data, and the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: accesso's Lee Cowie outlines how artificial intelligence and guest data are reshaping ticketing and in-park purchasing, with the goal of removing friction from every step of the guest journey. The piece aligns with a broader industry push toward frictionless experiences as a key differentiator for attractions operators. FEC operators evaluating ticketing and commerce platforms should consider how AI-driven personalization is rapidly becoming a baseline expectation.

articles.title: InPark Magazine's 'Frictionless Future' Issue Focuses on Removing Guest Experience Barriers
articles.summary: The latest issue of InPark Magazine explores how technology is being deployed across attractions to eliminate friction at every guest touchpoint, from ticketing and purchasing to in-park navigation and interactive experiences. Key contributors include accesso on commerce technology and Jora Vision on competitive socializing. FEC operators will find practical insights on the technology investments shaping guest satisfaction and operational efficiency.

articles.title: Jora Vision Expands Competitive Socializing Portfolio with New Skill-Based Concepts
articles.summary: Themed entertainment designer Jora Vision is growing its competitive socializing offering, developing new concepts built around skill-based games that blend physical challenge with social entertainment. Competitive socializing remains one of the fastest-growing FEC attraction categories, and Jora Vision's expanding portfolio signals continued innovation in the space. Operators looking to refresh or diversify their attraction mix should track Jora Vision's latest concepts.

articles.title: Launch Family Fun Center to Bring Arcade and Trampoline Park to Pensacola's Davis Highway
articles.summary: A new Launch family fun center featuring an arcade and trampoline park is set to open soon on Davis Highway in Pensacola, Florida, adding to the growing national Launch brand footprint. The opening reflects continued consumer demand for multi-attraction indoor entertainment in secondary markets. Local FEC operators in the region should evaluate the competitive impact of a branded, multi-activity venue entering their market.

articles.title: Major Kansas City Entertainment Center Closes After 13 Years
articles.summary: A large family entertainment center in Kansas City has permanently closed after 13 years of operation, highlighting the challenges of sustaining large-format venues over the long term in competitive markets. The closure serves as a reminder for FEC operators of the importance of ongoing reinvestment, format evolution, and brand relevance. Industry observers will be watching to see how the vacated space is repositioned.

articles.title: Six Flags St. Louis Rebrands as Mid America Adventure Under New Ownership
articles.summary: Six Flags St. Louis has officially been renamed Mid America Adventure following its transition to new owner Enchanted Parks, complete with a new logo and brand identity honoring the park's 55-year history. The rebrand signals a broader strategic shift as the park moves away from the Six Flags corporate umbrella and into independent regional park management. Operators and suppliers in the regional park sector will want to watch how the new ownership team repositions the venue.

articles.title: Six Flags St. Louis Becomes Mid America Adventure Following Ownership Transition
articles.summary: InPark confirms the renaming of Six Flags St. Louis to Mid America Adventure as Enchanted Parks completes its acquisition and establishes a new brand identity for the Missouri regional park. The transition is one of the more closely watched ownership changes in the regional amusement park sector this year. FEC operators and investors tracking consolidation and rebranding trends in the broader attractions industry should note this development.

articles.title: Endless Surf and Flowstate Partner to Bring AI Computer Vision to Surf Park Operations
articles.summary: Endless Surf and Flowstate have announced a strategic partnership combining customizable wave technology with AI-powered computer vision to create a more connected and personalized experience for surf park operators and guests. The integration enables real-time performance tracking and personalized data for surfers, raising the bar for guest engagement in the surf park segment. As surf parks grow in relevance to the broader active entertainment market, this technology partnership points to where the sector is heading.

articles.title: Lake Compounce Names Daniel LLanas as New General Manager
articles.summary: Lake Compounce Amusement & Water Park in Bristol, Connecticut has appointed Daniel LLanas as General Manager, bringing over 25 years of theme park, water park, and destination attraction leadership experience to America's oldest amusement park. Strong operational leadership is a critical differentiator for parks navigating post-pandemic attendance patterns and rising consumer expectations. The appointment may signal a renewed focus on operational performance and guest experience at the historic property.

articles.title: Six Flags and Warner Bros. Invest in Premium Interactive Horror with 'The Conjuring: Beyond Fear'
articles.summary: Six Flags, Plague Productions, and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences are collaborating on a premium interactive horror experience called The Conjuring: Beyond Fear, raising the stakes for Halloween programming in the regional park and FEC space. The investment in IP-driven, immersive horror reflects how operators are monetizing Halloween season with tiered premium experiences. FEC operators running escape rooms or seasonal horror events can draw direct lessons from this high-budget approach to interactive fear experiences.

articles.title: Six Flags Fiesta Texas Breaks Ground on World's Longest Family Launch Coaster
articles.summary: Six Flags Fiesta Texas has broken ground on Werewolf Gorge, billed as the world's longest family launch coaster and the largest single-attraction investment in the park's history, set to debut in 2027. The project signals continued major capital commitment to family-friendly thrill attractions in the regional park segment. Suppliers of ride systems, themed environments, and guest experience technology should take note of the scale and ambition of this project.

articles.title: Texas FEC Tornado Terry's Turns to GoFundMe as It Faces Closure
articles.summary: Tornado Terry's Family Amusement Center in the Keller-Roanoke area of northeast Fort Worth is seeking community support through a GoFundMe campaign in a last-ditch effort to stay open. The story highlights the financial fragility of independently owned FECs, particularly in markets facing increased competition from larger, better-capitalized entertainment venues. Independent operators may find the situation instructive as they evaluate their own financial resilience and community engagement strategies.

articles.title: New Family Entertainment Center Opens in Rock Springs, Wyoming
articles.summary: A new family entertainment center is opening in Rock Springs, Wyoming, expanding access to indoor entertainment options in a smaller western market. The opening reflects continued grassroots demand for FEC concepts in underserved secondary and tertiary markets across the US. Operators and franchisors looking at white-space expansion opportunities may find smaller markets like Rock Springs increasingly attractive.

articles.title: New Family Restaurant and Entertainment Experience Proposed for Grand Forks
articles.summary: A new family restaurant and entertainment concept has been proposed for the Franklin on Fourth development in Grand Forks, North Dakota, combining dining with family-focused entertainment. Food-and-fun hybrid concepts continue to proliferate in markets of all sizes as operators seek to drive longer dwell times and higher per-visit spending. The proposal illustrates the broadening geography of the eatertainment trend beyond major metros.

articles.title: UK Heatwaves Reshape Visitor Patterns at Indoor and Outdoor Attractions
articles.summary: A reflection on how unprecedented summer heat in the UK has affected visitor behavior at attractions, with outdoor venues challenged by extreme temperatures while indoor facilities see shifting demand patterns. The analysis is directly relevant for FEC operators navigating seasonal weather volatility and considering climate resilience in venue design and programming. Indoor entertainment centers may find growing competitive advantage as weather unpredictability increases.

articles.title: Parques Reunidos on How Leisure Venues Can Generate Meaningful Social Impact
articles.summary: European leisure park giant Parques Reunidos shares its perspective on how entertainment venues can deliver measurable social value alongside commercial performance. The piece is relevant for FEC operators looking to strengthen community positioning, ESG narratives, and local government relationships. As social impact becomes a growing factor in venue permitting and funding, operators who can articulate this value clearly will have an advantage.

articles.title: Alterface Celebrates 25 Years of Interactive Experience Design in Themed Entertainment
articles.summary: Interactive experience design specialist Alterface marks 25 years of creating shooting galleries, interactive dark rides, and gamified attractions for major theme parks and entertainment venues worldwide. Their work on invisible technology — where guests engage fully without needing instructions — is directly applicable to FEC operators designing arcade and interactive attraction areas. The milestone retrospective offers valuable design philosophy for operators investing in next-generation interactive attractions.

articles.title: Big Break Foundation: Inclusion and Accessibility Are Good for FEC Business
articles.summary: A column from the Big Break Foundation argues that genuine inclusion and accessibility in attractions is not only a moral imperative but also a sound business strategy that broadens the addressable customer base. For FEC operators, designing for accessibility — from physical layout to sensory-friendly programming — can meaningfully increase visits and guest satisfaction. The piece provides a practical framework for thinking about DEI and accessibility as operational and revenue levers.
